intro: Every word this module’s exercises use, on one deck of flashcards: 369 cards, 153 of them nouns. The vocabulary of this module is the language of society, work, environment and science, much of it abstract nouns in -ung, -heit, -keit and -ion, from the themes Gesellschaft & Politik, Arbeit & Wirtschaft, Medien & Kommunikation, Konsum. Write the German, choose it from four options, or flip the card and rate yourself. A word you miss comes back later in the same run, and stays in your weak words until you get it right three times in a row.
tips[0].title: Suffixes give the gender away
tips[0].text: Most abstract nouns are feminine because of their suffix: -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion and -tät always take die. Use the suffix, not memory, when you are unsure.
tips[0].check.why: Nouns ending in -schaft are always feminine.
tips[1].title: Reporting verbs with their partners
tips[1].text: behaupten, betonen, erklären, hinzufügen introduce what someone said; the report itself goes into the Konjunktiv I: er sei, sie habe, man werde.
tips[1].check.why: Reported speech after behaupten: Konjunktiv I, er wisse.
tips[2].title: Politics nouns: watch the plural
tips[2].text: die Steuern is usually plural (taxes); die Mehrheit and die Minderheit have regular -en plurals; das Gesetz takes -e: die Gesetze.
tips[2].check.why: das Gesetz, die Gesetze: the plural ending is -e.
remember[0]: Never say a noun without its article, not even in your head.
remember[1]: Miss a word? It comes back in the same run. Three correct answers in a row take it off the weak list.
remember[2]: Verbs and adjectives have no article: type them as they stand, like "beschließen".
hook: Learn the words of news, work and society with their articles, so abstract nouns stop being a guessing game.
